candidates.exact_span: For the purposes of this Part, significant noncompliance shall be determined based upon the more stringent of either criteria established at 40 CFR Part 403.8(f)(2)(viii) [rev. 10/14/05] or criteria established in the approved POTW pretreatment program.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which industrial users count as in significant noncompliance depends on whether federal 403.8(f)(2)(viii) criteria or the approved local pretreatment program criteria apply and which is more stringent; that classification affects which users must be listed and what monitoring/reporting obligations are treated as triggered, and whether missing or borderline evidence is classified as established noncompliance versus unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall prepare annually a list of Industrial Users which during the preceding twelve months were in significant noncompliance with applicable pretreatment requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes an annual monitoring/reporting obligation keyed to the preceding twelve-month window; interpretation of that rolling period and of 'significant noncompliance' changes which users and time spans are in scope for FY2025 obligation evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: An updated list of all significant industrial users and identify which Industrial Users are Non-Significant Categorical Industrial Users (NSCIUs) or Middle Tier CIUs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: User tier classification (SIU vs NSCIU vs Middle Tier CIU) governs which pretreatment monitoring and reporting requirements are applicable; misclassification would change which requirements are evaluated as required.

candidates.exact_span: Industrial Users subject to categorical Pretreatment Standards that are subject to reduced monitoring and reporting requirements under 40 CFR 403.12(e)(2) & (3);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Eligibility for reduced monitoring under 403.12(e)(2) and (3) determines whether ordinary monitoring was required; different interpretations change whether a no-result period is conditional non-requirement versus missing required evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Industrial Users subject to the following categorical Pretreatment Standards [Organic Chemicals, Plastics, and Synthetic Fibers (OCPSF) (40 CFR part 414), Petroleum Refining (40 CFR part 419), and Pesticide Chemicals (40 CFR part 455)] and for which the Control Authority has chosen to use the concentration-based standards rather than converting them to flow-based mass standards as allowed at 40 CFR 403.6(c)(6);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the Control Authority elected concentration-based standards instead of flow-based mass standards under 403.6(c)(6) determines whether enforceable limits are expressed and compared as concentration or mass, changing the applicable numeric limit for compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: Categorical Industrial Users subject to concentration-based standards for which the Control Authority has chosen to convert the concentration-based standards to equivalent mass limits, as allowed at 40 CFR 403.6(c)(5);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Election to convert concentration-based categorical standards to equivalent mass limits under 403.6(c)(5) changes the numeric form of the enforceable limit used in exceedance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: General Control Mechanisms used for similar groups of SIUs along with the substantially similar types of operations and the types of wastes that are the same, for each separate General Control Mechanism, as allowed at 40 CFR 403.8(f)(1)(iii);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Grouping of SIUs under General Control Mechanisms affects which consolidated or shared monitoring and control requirements apply to individual users; scope of 'substantially similar' operations and wastes changes evaluated obligations.

candidates.exact_span: Best Management Practices or Pollution Prevention alternatives required by a categorical Pretreatment Standard or as a local limit requirement
candidates.computation_change_reason: BMP or pollution-prevention alternatives may substitute for or supplement numeric pretreatment limits and standard monitoring; whether a requirement is framed as a local limit or an alternative compliance pathway changes which enforceable numeric limits apply and which monitoring is required.
